title: Four and a Half Friends
subtitle: Ladies and gentlemen, kindly take your seats. The shadow play is about to begin!

items.text: The train rocks as it plows through the winter storm.
The investigator lets her vision glaze over the scene beyond the window, still pondering the meaning of the conductress's badge.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: She handed it over so naturally, as if she had done it countless times.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Plus, it appears she's encountered someone from the Foundation before. I am forced to conclude that our conductress is hiding something from me.
She pulls a pocket watch from her coat and flicks it open.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: They've been gone for a while now. Well ...
Then she looks around the room.
Thanks to the conductress's fine administrative processes, every file is simple to find.
From timetables to station logs, everything is within reach.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: These files are just sitting out on the table. Do they have no sense of confidentiality?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: An easily laid clue is often a trap, though. This could be bait. Better act cautiously.
The investigator shakes her head, casting the thought aside.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I apologize for keeping you.
Corvus enters and returns to her sofa; her loyal stewardess follows in behind.
She takes stock of the room, confirming that nothing has changed since she left.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Aima has placed your luggage at your seat. No need to worry; nothing has ever gone missing from the "Danube Dawn."

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: You've waited for some time. Where were we?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: The Foundation, your vampire, and this investigation you mentioned.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: To rule out any threat, I need to verify every passenger on board, carriage by carriage.
The investigator shifts tactics, speaking more directly.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: That would be controversial, especially in the midst of this war. I fear it may cause unnecessary disturbances.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I'm sure neither of us would like a repeat of the incident from before.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I apologize, but my mission parameters are clear. You've misunderstood my intent; this was a notification, not a negotiation.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: In that case, I will need to see some formal authorization.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I won't allow someone to disturb the peace of my passengers just because they claim it to be necessary.
She arches a brow, certain that the investigator doesn't have the authorization.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I fear that authorization is still little more than a draft on their desk—the "joys of bureaucracy."

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But as you seem to be a fan of red tape, if you refuse to cooperate, regulations state that it is within my power ...
She pauses to draw out the effect.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: To stop the "Danube Dawn."

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Stop the train? No.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Indeed. I am fully within my authority to stop this train at any time to conduct an investigation.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: I understand, but it could inconvenience our passengers.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Just the passengers?
Aima opens her mouth, then closes it again, glancing at the conductress.
Corvus stands and pats her on the shoulder.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I have one stipulation that my stewardess and I accompany you during your inspection.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: As you wish. I assure you the process will be carried out with openness and transparency.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: If the purpose is likewise open and transparent, yes.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Naturally, Conductress, I have told you everything—as far as I'm permitted, at least.
The investigator maintains a practiced, businesslike smile as she extends her hand.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: There is no time to lose. Let's get started.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Glad we could come to an agreement, Conductress.
Seating Carriage
Announcements, explanations, records ... their "cooperation" continues smoothly.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: How many carriages left?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Um, except the locomotive, the brake van, our compartment, two registered, and this one we're registering ...

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Twelve minus three, then minus two, then minus one.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Six carriages to go.
Semmelweis answers with a subdued smile.

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: Conductress, Ms. Aima, I need your help. Two of my students have gone missing.
A worried lady approaches, concern evident on her brow.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Please remain calm, madam. How long have they been missing? Could you describe them in detail?

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: The two of them are about this tall. The little girl always carries a doll with her, and the boy has short, brown curly hair.

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: I lost sight of them in the dining car about half an hour ago. Seems they've taken this train as some sort of playground.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Conductress, they sound like the little boy and girl we met just now.
She notes down each description carefully, attentive to all the passengers.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Ah, Rubuska's "familiars."

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Look behind you, madam. Are these your students?
Following the conductress's words, all eyes turn to the children at the back.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: After the glorious Count Arnold V came my grandfather Savonovic!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Grandfather Savonovic brought the whole family north of the Danube and built Arges Mill—er, I mean, Arges Castle!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: He lived to be 165 years old.

items.speaker: Children
items.text: *snore*
The girl eagerly continues her tales, unaware and unconcerned that her audience has drifted off to sleep.

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: William! Annabelle! You can't go messing about yourselves like this!
The governess storms over, skirt swaying wider than usual, appearing almost like a bowling ball rolling down the aisle.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Mmm. Hm? Ah!

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: M-Ms. Dorothy! Uh-oh.
The children jolt awake, Annabelle springing from Rubuska's lap.

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: Annabelle! You get back here right now! You should know better than to associate with that kind of company.

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: That goes for you too, William! Come on, quickly!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: That ... that kind of company?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Is she talking about me?
From her sharp gaze, Rubuska realizes the difference in their clothes.
A hand lands on her shoulder, breaking her thought.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: We meet again, "old pal." We're here to register your information if you might spare the time.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: If I said I couldn't, would you let me go?

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: I suggest you do a thorough check on her background. I suspect she could be a trafficker!

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: No, Ms. Dorothy, I was lost, a-and Rubuska helped me!

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: How many times have I told you? You are a young lady of a certain stature. It won't do to get too close to this riff-raff.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Riff-raff? Hey, lady, what do you mean?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: A-Apologies, madam, but this is just a simple passenger registration.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: No need to worry, Ms. Rubuska. We just have a few simple questions for you. Let's see. Um, what are you?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I'm Rubuska!
She straightens her back and speaks firmly.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Um, sorry, perhaps I wasn't clear. I mean your lineage.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: L-Lineage. Oh, sure, I'm Th-Thermanikian.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Let's hurry this along. Not your name, nor your place of birth, nor gender.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Arcanist or human?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Oh! Um, then, I guess I'm ...

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: There is no third option.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Wow, how do you know? Alright! I, I'm—
The girl falters, eyes dodging, but it's William that leaps to explain.

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: She's our vampire boss; of course she's an arcanist.

items.speaker: Dorothy
items.text: Silence, William! Who taught you to say such things?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Oh!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Ha, hahaha, ah, I was just messing around with the kids.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Didn't you ever play make-believe when you were young? Vampires, werewolves, Rusalka ...

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I did not.
The conductress coldly interrupts her.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Given these extraordinary times, I'll ask that there be no more such make-believe on the train.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I won't do it again, I swear.
She exhales, but Annabelle, now awake and confused, speaks up.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: But you are a vampire, Rubuska.
The air stills.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: You don't have a shadow. You showed us. And real vampires don't have shadows, right?

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Vampires are really, really strong, and Rubuska is a good vampire. S-So you should all be nice to her!
She gathers her courage, standing firm even under the governess's glare, her voice quiet but sure as she challenges their attitude.
The crowd looks down to the finely embroidered carpet beneath the girl's feet and fails to find her shadow.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: She's right. She really has no shadow.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Uh-oh.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: You call this "messing around"?
The patchwork conductress takes a step forward, her towering figure making the children stumble back in fear.
Her hand rests once more on Rubuska's shoulder, firm yet proper.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: You're going to have to come with us.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I'm afraid that "Danube Dawn" security protocol dictates an immediate closed interrogation.
